acceptance_criteria: A clean supported Agent Plugin installation can be agent-initialized and capture a canonical goal without manual form filling.
An execution run can prioritize, unblock, verify, checkpoint, and cycle across durable goals without losing state.
Unsupported capabilities and human-only decisions become explicit categorized blockers rather than invented behavior.
Supported coding agents receive concise, discoverable Agent Plugin workflow semantics.
Tests prove Agent Plugin packaging and marketplace discovery, backend invariants, fast observable feedback, and prompt-budget accounting.
beneficiaries: developers delegating long-running project work to coding agents
constraints: Remain primarily agent-driven and keep deterministic scripts narrow and cross-platform.
Do not silently dual-write, fail over, invent user decisions, or expose secrets.
Keep installed prompts distilled and prompt counts current.
Use available subscription capacity to advance evidenced project goals and safe valuable backlog work; do not let quota maximization override value, safety, or user authority.
Keep Codex and Claude Code distributions generated from shared canonical sources; claim platform support only after platform-native validation and install/discovery/workflow acceptance evidence.

kpis.baseline: GitHub Issues are the canonical backend.
kpis.name: Canonical goal integrity
kpis.target: Zero known lost or duplicated canonical goals.
kpis.why: Lost or duplicated goal truth defeats autonomous execution.

kpis.evidence: Timed supported-platform plugin installation and initialization acceptance run.
kpis.name: Time to usable backlog
kpis.target: Supported plugin install to initialized, capturable backlog in under 10 minutes.

kpis.evidence: Goal histories and categorized blocker records.
kpis.name: Autonomous workflow transitions
kpis.target: At least 80% of eligible workflow transitions need no unscheduled human input.
kpis.why: Measures whether agents can continue without unscheduled intervention.

non_goals: Guarantee capabilities that Codex does not expose.
Restore or maintain the retired per-project installer, or maintain divergent Codex and Claude Code workflow implementations.
Spend tokens on work with no evidenced link to project value.
charter.outcome: ZzzOps lets supported coding agents manage long-term project work autonomously with durable state, minimal babysitting, and explicit human control.
charter.precedence: user authority and safety, correctness, privacy, verified project value, autonomy, then prompt savings
unacceptable_tradeoffs: More autonomy at the expense of user health, privacy, repository safety, or observable correctness.
Lower prompt cost by omitting state required for safe resumption or human control.
charter.why_it_matters: Users can stop supervising agents late into the night without losing progress, priorities, blockers, or available work.

evidence.finding: The existing confirmed charter defines the outcome, KPIs, acceptance criteria, and value constraints.

Repository guidance requires dev-based per-goal implementation and PRs, Conventional Commits, human review, owner-only main releases, prompt-budget checks, observable work, and reviewed PROJECT policy as the operational source of truth.
GitHub Issues are enabled for david-rzepa/zzzops and the authenticated user has ADMIN permission.
Health reminders were removed and GitHub Issues is now the only supported canonical goal backend.
User decisions require review-ready dependency stacking, a brief bounded human-unblock watch, and artifact-specific verification without recursive documentation or test meta-tests.
Communication style is reviewed project policy; outcome-first, low-technical-detail updates are the user's preferred ZzzOps default and may be overridden by explicit project policy.

User selected bounded refill for documentation, test coverage, and non-behavioral code quality, completed dependencies before writable implementation, read-only advance investigation, and up to three size-aware workers with clean worktree removal or reuse.

Use chained per-goal PRs from exact reviewed checkpoints; interview only during capture at standard adaptive depth with the requesting user as sole stakeholder; execute unattended with durable blockers; capture test-discovered out-of-scope bugs as blocked goals; enable privacy-safe execution reports.

Authorization to execute a goal includes diagnosing and repairing CI failures caused by that goal's own changes; do not ask for separate fix approval unless the repair expands scope or needs new authority.
Adopt Agent Plugins v1 for Codex, remove the legacy installer and Claude v2 support, and direct Claude users to final legacy release v1.2.0.
Disable automated design authority; require explicit user direction for design choices.

Support generated, acceptance-gated Claude Code plugin artifacts derived from shared canonical sources; preserve removal of the retired per-project installer and prohibit divergent platform implementations.

Prefer GitHub-native stacked pull requests when the official capability is installed and stack membership can be verified; require approval before installing or upgrading host tooling, and explicitly use chained pull requests when native stacking is declined, unavailable, or unverified.

sections.default_origin: user decision and current product scope
sections.rationale: GitHub capability is usable and completed issue #81 made it the only supported authority.

tradeoffs.github_issues: shared native issue queue requiring GitHub access

sections.title: Canonical goal backend

sections.decision: Use one branch and PR per goal. Prefer GitHub-native stacked PRs when the official capability is installed and provider stack membership is verified; otherwise explicitly use chained PRs from exact reviewed checkpoints. Merge in dependency order, use Conventional Commits, collect human PR approval when safe work is exhausted, and retain owner-only main releases.
sections.rationale: The user selected GitHub-native stacked PRs as the preferred mode and named chained PRs as the safe fallback, while retaining per-goal review units, checks, ordered integration, and human authority.
sections.title: Git, review, and release

sections.decision: Continue across actionable goals under reviewed dependency and resource policy, incorporate newly captured goals at the next safe checkpoint, and persist unanswered questions without live interviewing, notification, polling, or waiting.
sections.rationale: Execution is unattended; durable blockers preserve every consequential request without requiring a live user.
sections.title: Execution and work continuation

sections.decision: Require artifact-appropriate observable evidence in small chunks; documentation and test cases need no recursive tests, while product behavior and reusable test infrastructure require direct verification.
sections.rationale: Root instructions forbid unobservable implementation and unsanctioned test-bug fixes.
sections.title: Verification and testing

sections.decision: Preserve behavior unless a goal explicitly authorizes a behavior change.
sections.rationale: A bounded self-review prevents unrelated cleanup from expanding work.
sections.title: Code-quality and refactoring boundaries

sections.decision: Use project-native tooling; do not hand-edit generated or dependency-owned files; generate supported platform distributions from shared canonical sources and verify them with platform-native validation and acceptance evidence.
sections.rationale: Keeps deterministic mechanics portable, ownership clear, and Codex/Claude support aligned without divergent implementations.
sections.title: Dependencies, tooling, and generated artifacts

sections.decision: Repository policy may tighten but never weaken safety and authority boundaries.
sections.rationale: The charter expressly forbids secret exposure and invented authority.
sections.title: Security, privacy, secrets, and compliance

sections.decision: Follow evidenced repository documentation and style conventions; use outcome-first, low-technical-detail user updates by default while allowing explicit project policy to override the style.
sections.default_origin: repository policy and user-preferred ZzzOps default
sections.rationale: Repository instructions require prompt-budget updates, and the user selected concise actionable communication as this project's default without making it universal policy.
sections.title: Documentation and style

sections.decision: Do not deploy without authority; choose bounded parallelism from the deterministic tracked-file repository size.
sections.rationale: Repository release policy restricts main updates, while the tracked tree is below 100 MB and the user selected size-aware parallel defaults.
sections.title: Deployment, environment, and resources

sections.rationale: Balance production-oriented specification and verification with automatic escalation for high-risk work.
sections.title: Engineering rigor

sections.rationale: Require durable goal context for substantial agent work while preserving narrow administration and read-only exemptions.
sections.title: ZzzOps workflow adherence

sections.decision: Interview adaptively during goal capture at the reviewed depth; treat the requesting user as the sole stakeholder; execute unattended by persisting consequential questions as durable blockers; repair in-scope CI failures without another approval; record privacy-safe execution reports; refill valuable bounded work; and use up to three size-aware workers.
sections.default_origin: user-selected ZzzOps defaults and project policy
sections.rationale: This separates present-user requirements discovery from unattended execution while preserving durable control, chained progress, and privacy-safe machinery feedback.
sections.title: Autonomy, approvals, and parallelism

sections.rationale: Require explicit user direction for design choices; unattended execution persists them as durable blockers.
